record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  note N [--correcting TIME]     a noted block in N's history, N unchanged; needs
                                 --note; refused when the history holds it already.
                                 TIME: 2026-10-13 19:07Z, or 2nd 2026-10-14 04:41Z
      record.py note P-25 --from 'positions-audit/full/evidence/corrections-c1.md#History lines the tool cannot write' --note 'his message behind the text: 2026-09-26T08:01:03.475Z, ...'
      record.py note P-7 --correcting '2026-10-13 19:07Z' --commit b87a17de5 --note 'that block names bc8902f47, ...'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
`remove F-90`; `merge F-91 into F-87`; `note F-87`, or `note F-87 correcting
TIME`, a noted block. Each may be followed by one indented provenance line of
its own:
`  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: HASH; by: WHO; note: WHY`. Blank lines and
`<!-- -->` comments are ignored. An entry line equal to the entry is skipped:
to add to its history, write `note F-87`. A note whose block the history holds
already, all but its time, is skipped too, so a file run twice writes nothing
twice. One call writes one block per entry, so an entry is noted, or changed,
once in a file.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

# Facts on record

18:- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes, so a division by zero elsewhere ends the run (rows 336, 848). Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, and for a helper by `tests/NativeHelperRaiseWalk.fss` and `tests/ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk.fss`. 30:- F-32 **The compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes, the Java classes that most of the one library's native bindings name: of its 449 live bindings, 428 name one.** A native binding is a library body `builtinPrimitive("…")`; its string names a glue class, which takes walk's boxed values, or a static helper of `nativeHelpers/`, over plain Java values, which both paths call (F-298; F-299 holds the 21 that name one). # Rung K, rung-natives-choose: record lines for the gather

## Findings

1. **Trait `ZZ32`'s and trait `ZZ64`'s `CHOOSE` now name their helpers on both paths, and the helpers are exact and keep no shared state.**
   - Claim: `opr CHOOSE` names `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intOverflowingChoose` in trait `ZZ32` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:789`) and `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleLongArith.longOverflowingChoose` in trait `ZZ64` (`:882`). Each helper gives the binomial coefficient, 0 where `k < 0` or `k > n`, and `IntegerOverflow` exactly where the coefficient does not fit its type. Each slow-path call has its own scratch array.
   - Conditions: on the tree of `00e620a3f`. Walk calls the helpers through these bindings. The compiled path calls them through the prelude (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:741`, `:652`), and also, through the `ZZ64` helper, for `NN32` (`:806`, `simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:80-82`). It reaches the one library's bindings only after the switch-over.
   - Evidence: the fix is at `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java:162-163` and `:210-213`, and `simpleLongArith.java:136-137` and `:183-186`. The tests pass on the fix and fail on the base:
     - `harness-one.sh` on the base: 'Wrapped exception java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 15 out of bounds for length 15', '... Index 32 out of bounds for length 32', 'Tests run: 5,  Failures: 2'. On the fix: 'OK (5 tests)'.
     - `junit.sh` on the base: 'Tests run: 7,  Failures: 3'. On the fix: 'OK (7 tests)'.

Climb batch 24, rung G, on `wip/rung-codegen-where` from `b0f6cd6b7`. The detail of every line below is in `REPORT.md` beside this file, by section.

## Findings

1. **The code generator compiles a function, method, object or trait declaration whose own header carries a `where` clause, and emits nothing for the clause.** Conditions: the program passes the compiled checker, which checks the clause's constraints; the declaration has no contract. Evidence: the three guards' `header.getWhereClause().isNone() &&` conditions are deleted (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:2967`, `:4107`, `:5027` at `b0f6cd6b7`); `compiler_tests/WhereBoundFunctionCompiled`, `WhereBoundMethodCompiled`, `WhereBoundObjectCompiled`, `WhereBoundTraitMethodCompiled` and `ComprisesWhereFunctionalMethodCompiled` fail on the base at a guard ('Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl. node = g[\U\](u:U):String', 'Can't compile ObjectDecl Wrap', 'Can't compile TraitDecl AnyBox') and pass after (`junit.sh final`, 'OK (18 tests)'). The forms: a function's condition on its static parameter; a method's condition on its trait's or object's parameter, abstract in the trait and given in the object (`BoundedRange.atMost`'s form), with a body in the object (`SumReduction`'s `distribute`'s form), or with a body in the trait, dotted or functional; a generic method's condition on its own parameter; an object's own clause; a trait whose `comprises` clause lists a generic object at a `where`-clause type variable, its functional methods' bodies in the trait (`AnyList`'s form). ## Sentences made false

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4466-4472`, the entry "A native binding that names a static helper", its Effect: "Twenty-one of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper: nineteen of the trait ℤ32, … and the getters asString and asExprString of the interpreter's object Int." - `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4466-4473`, the Appendix I entry "A native binding that names a static helper", its Effect: "Twenty-one of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper: nineteen of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, ..." and "The other 428 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call." With this rung alone, 57 name a helper and 392 a glue class.
- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4483-4486`, the same Effect: "\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD}, the three on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, and \EXP{\div} on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, which still name glue classes, end the run with a Java exception at a divisor of zero (row~336 ...)": `ZZ64`'s `DIV` and `ZZ`'s `DIV` now throw `DivisionByZero`; `ZZ32`'s `REM` and `MOD` and `ZZ64`'s `REM` and `MOD` still end the run. The gather rewrites the Effect (fork 7).
- Row 336's claim, "`DIV`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero on `ZZ64`, and `DIV` by zero on `ZZ` end the run": rewritten in `record.md`.
- F-32's counts, "of its 449 live bindings, 428 name one" (a glue class), and F-299's "21 of the one library's 449 live bindings name one" (a helper) with its list of the 21: with this rung, 392 and 57.

`opr-overview.tex:164-165` becomes true for `ZZ64`'s and `ZZ`'s `DIV`. No `\revision` or `\note{}` box of the specification speaks of walk's integer division by zero (`grep -rn -i 'by zero' Specification/ --include=*.tex` names only the listings, the operators chapter and the Appendix I entry). The `fortress-repo` skill's `references/interpreter.md`, "Natives", "`ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero raises `DivisionByZero` in this way.", stays true and could name `ZZ64` and `ZZ` (the record's "Revival change").

On this rung's tree, 29 of the 449 bindings name a helper and 420 a glue class. These sentences are made false:

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4466`: "Twenty-one of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper: nineteen of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, … and the getters \VAR{asString} and \VAR{asExprString} of the interpreter's object \TYP{Int}." This is the gather's to correct (fork 7).
- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4473`: "The other 428 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call." This is the gather's to correct (fork 7).
- F-32's title, "of its 449 live bindings, 428 name one", and its clause "F-299 holds the 21 that name one".
- F-299's title, "21 of the one library's 449 live bindings name one", and its sentence "The 21: 19 of trait `ZZ32`'s operators and functions … and `Int`'s `asString` and `asExprString` …; the other 428 still name glue classes".

`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-29`, `builtinPrimitive`'s comment, holds no count and stays true.

=== W
## Sentences made false

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4493-4498`, in the entry "A native binding that names a static helper", Effect: "The interpreter reads the \KWD{self} of a method only by the helper's Java type, since it is not told the type that declares the method: a helper bound in a method of a type that no Java type carries, as a program's own object, is not refused, and its call passes the object as that Java type reads it, the name of its type to a helper over \TYP{String} (row~847 of the revival's gap ledger)." The gather rewrites it (fork 7). What stays true: a dotted method of a generic trait or object is refused only at its instance (NEW-W-1).
- `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:134`, F-299: "It reads a method's `self` only by the helper's Java type, so a binding in a method of a program's own type loads (row 847)." Its citation `NativeApp.java:194-201` is now `:200-207`.
- `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/interpreter.md:103`, "Natives": "Walk does not check `self`. It passes `self` as the helper's first Java parameter, read as that parameter's Java type. So a binding in a method of a program's own type loads, and a `String` parameter receives the type's name (ledger row 847)." The list above it (`:97-101`) lacks the new refusal, 'no Java type carries T, the type of self.', and the self-first rule. `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/sources.md:941` gives "`self` not checked" and `XXXNativeHelperUncarriedSelfWalk` as that part's source.
- Still true: `FortressBuiltin.fsi:19`, "%self% first", now true of `self` as well; `explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:445`, whose citations `NativeApp.java:194-201` and `:164-223` are now `:200-207` and `:164-229`; `compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:17`.

=== G
## 7. Sentences made false

The specification (Appendix I Effects; the gather corrects them, since the rung edits no `Specification/` file):

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:255-257`, entry "Conditional extension", Effect: "The code generator compiles a declaration whose \KWD{extends} clause has such a clause; it refuses one that carries a \KWD{where} clause of its own (row~701)." Its second half is false.
- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1672-1673`, entry "The traits that extend a closed trait", Effect: "The code generator does not yet compile a trait with a \KWD{where} clause or read a size off an argument at a call (rows~307 and~701)." Its first half is false; the second stays true (row 307).
- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4268-4271`, entry "The index type of a subscript", Effect: "The code generator refuses a method with a \KWD{where} clause of its own (row~701 of the revival's gap ledger), so after the switch-over \TYP{BoundedRange}'s \VAR{atMost} waits on that row, beside the two \VAR{distribute} methods of \library's sum reduction." False.

The record and the skill (the gather's and the skill writer's):

- F-181 (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:249`): "The code generator refuses every function, method, object and trait declaration that carries a `where` clause in its own header" (record.md gives its rewrite).
- F-34 (`FACTS.md:31`): "the kinds include … a header `where` clause (row 701)", a measurement at `2bff2fe23`; the kind is gone from the code generator.
- F-281 (`FACTS.md:120`): "such a program still stops in the code generator (row 812; row 701)": row 701's half is false; row 812's stands where a listed generic type gives a member's body.
- F-270 (`FACTS.md:206`): "The code generator does not compile such a trait: "Can't compile TraitDecl NatParamT" (row 307; `compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun`).": the trait compiles, and the call that opens its size fails verification (added by the skeptic, `SKEPTIC.md`).
- P-151 (`POSITIONS.md:63`): "Row 701: the code generator's half."
- P-156 (`POSITIONS.md:67`): "the code generator refuses a `where` clause in a declaration's header", and "after the switch-over the code generator's refusal of a method with a `where` clause stops it too, as it stops `SumReduction`'s two `distribute`s (row 701)".
- `PLAN.md:59`: "a header `where` clause (row 701)" among the code generator's kinds; `PLAN.md:249`: "and the code generator's half (row 701), in phase 4 before the names batch".
- The skill: `references/revival-changes.md:67`, "The code generator refuses a declaration with a `where` clause of its own (row 701)."; `references/compiler.md:44`, "It also refuses a function, method, object or trait declaration with a `where` clause of its own"; `references/compiler.md:103`, "only the checker reads it, and the code generator refuses such a declaration (ledger row 701)"; `references/compiler.md:110`, "A program that declares such a trait does not compile: the code generator refuses the trait's `where` clause (ledger row 701)."
- Row 701's claim (record.md gives its new line); row 812's claim, "before its refusal of a `where` clause (row 701)", and its notes' "With the member in the object only, row 701's 'Can't compile TraitDecl'" (record.md gives its new line); row 677's notes, "The reproducer `XXXWhereBoundChecker` now stops in the code generator and is keyed on row 701's wall." (record.md gives its new line, the row staying `FIXED`); row 307's notes, "To run, the code generator must compile `NatParam`, whose `comprises` clause binds a `where`-clause size … (row 701)" (record.md gives its new line).

=== H
## 8. Sentences made false

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4466-4473`, the Effect of "A native binding that names a static helper": "Twenty-one of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper: …" and "The other 428 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call." \item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 10~October 2026 that every native binding of \library\
keeps the library's own form, a body that is exactly a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, and that its string names a static helper of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, the compiled code's own
helpers, in place of a glue class, which takes the interpreter's values and
which the compiled code cannot call.
The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and the type checker checks each
moved binding against its helper's Java signature from the step that moves it.
The alternative not taken was \KWD{import} \KWD{java} declarations written in
the source files of \library, the compiler's own form for its natives, which
the interpreter does not run.
A reversal would restore the original comment, put the moved bindings back on
their glue classes, and leave the compiled code without a binding of the
natives of \library\ that it can call.

\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-natives-walk/decision-record.md}

\TYP{IntegerOverflow} (row~521 of the revival's gap ledger).

content.content:
# Keeping the record

How workers read the record, and edit it when a brief asks, is `fortress-repo`'s records part.

**history**
: `FACTS-history.md` or `POSITIONS-history.md`. Under each number, one block per change: a provenance line (the time, the kind of change, the report section, the commit, who, why) and the line as it stood before.

**pointer**
: Another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, with a few words on its subject: "It builds P-48, on a type parameter that a call does not fix."

**pass**
: Your rewrite of what a worker wrote into entries of the form below.

## What an entry is

An entry reads on its own. A reader who knows the language, or can look it up in the `fortress-repo` skill, can tell what it says without the conversation or the batch behind it. The entry lets a worker or you act right without opening the report, and says when the report is needed. Its number is permanent and never reused. Its title and text are rewritten freely, since the number is the key.

- A FACTS entry holds, after its number and a bold title that states the fact: what is established now, and under which conditions; what it means for the work, such as what it blocks or which row or decision it bears on; its evidence: the test that gates it, or its source, and whether it was observed, read in the code or inferred; the decision it builds, by number and subject; and the report section that holds the detail.
- A POSITIONS entry holds, after its number and a bold title: what the curator decided about the project, and why, in one or two sentences; where it applies; and what it requires of the work. It may point to a fact that it rests on, in the sentence that needs it. `P-48+` finds every fact that points to it.
- POSITIONS holds only the curator's decisions. A choice that a worker made and landed without the curator's word is a fact about the tree. Its FACTS entry says that a worker chose it, and its review-queue item names that entry.
- An entry states the present, or what holds for all time. It holds no plan and no status: no state words such as "Built." or "Still to build:", no PLAN phase or item, no review-queue item, and no words that it waits for the curator's review. PLAN and the review queue name the entries that their items concern.
- If the tree does not yet do what a decision or the team's design asks, the missing part is a row of the gap ledger. The entry may name it as "row N", with a few words on what the row holds. In an entry, "row N" always names a row of the gap ledger.
- A pointer that stays in an entry carries a few words on what it holds, such as a ledger row's subject. A bare list of numbers goes to the history.
- A handle that only made sense in a past conversation, such as "answer 9", goes to the history.
- Quote the curator only where the exact words are the decision. Otherwise condense the words into the position, keeping the part of the rule that cuts. Check the condensed text against the words before you write it. The dictated words go to the history, with their time.
- A count that each landing changes has one entry with its current value, what it counts, the kinds with the largest share, and how to read a move. Other entries give its number. A count from one measurement says so.
- An entry holds one claim that can be kept up to date on its own, with its conditions, exceptions and evidence. Split an entry when its claims answer different questions and change apart. Before you split, look for an entry that already holds the claim, and move the text there. After a split, grep the record for the old number, and repoint each pointer that meant the claim that moved.
- If several entries together establish a conclusion that workers keep working out again, make it a sentence of the entry that owns its subject, with pointers to the entries it rests on. The pass updates it when one of them changes. Add a new entry only if no entry owns it. Leave a conclusion nobody has checked in its report, out of the entries.
- Keep an entry near 600 characters. This is a check, not a cap, and no reason to split: an entry may pass it if a question below keeps a sentence.
- Write halfway to ASD-STE100.

Ask of each sentence, and act on the answer:

1. Would the reader do otherwise without it? Keep it.
2. Would the reader misread another sentence without it? Keep it.
3. Does it tell how the fact came about: a date, a batch, a correction? Move it to the history.
4. Is it detail needed only while doing the work: a line number, a list of sites, a timing? Leave it in the report, and name the section.
5. Does another entry or a skill say it? Give that entry's number, or the skill's part.
6. Can a reader new to the project follow every word? Name the kind of each count.

In a consolidation of FACTS, judge each entry by six checks. Mark each one pass, fail, or unresolved where evidence is still needed, and quote the passage that fails:

- Scope: the title and the text agree on the path, the conditions and the limits, and claim no more than the evidence shows.
- Present meaning: a reader can tell the current property, or a measurement bounded to its day, without rebuilding a batch's work.
- Evidence: the cited support exists and holds the claim, and the entry states the kind of its evidence and its uncertainty.
- Comprehension: a reader can restate the fact and what it means. Subjects, referents and terms are plain.
- Ownership: the entry has one subject. No repair history or copied count hides it.
- Consistency: entries on the same subject agree, or state their different scopes or their conflict.

An entry that fails scope, evidence or consistency is not kept as it stands: reword it to what its support holds, or investigate where the support is unresolved. A fail of comprehension or ownership asks for a rewrite. Give no score: good prose does not make up for an unsupported claim. Then give the entry one disposition:

- keep: every check passes;
- reword: the meaning holds, but the wording or the stated scope fails;
- reorganize: move detail out, merge the entry into its owner, or split it;
- investigate: the support or the consistency is unresolved. Settle that narrow question before any new wording, and do not delete the fact meanwhile.

Before you write or check the first entries of a consolidation, read the five worked examples: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-rule-draft.md#Worked examples'`, a large read.

import sys, re
# fx.py FILE-WITH-RECORD ID OUT old new [old new ...]: take the line of entry/row ID, replace each old (exactly once) by new, write OUT
src, ident, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
pairs = sys.argv[4:]
lines = open(src, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
if ident.startswith('F-') or ident.startswith('P-'):
    cand = [l for l in lines if l.startswith('- ' + ident + ' ')]
else:
    cand = [l for l in lines if re.match(r'^\| ' + re.escape(ident) + r' \|', l)]
assert len(cand) == 1, (ident, len(cand))
line = cand[0]
for i in range(0, len(pairs), 2):
    o, n = pairs[i], pairs[i+1]
    c = line.count(o)
    assert c == 1, ('count', c, o)
    line = line.replace(o, n)
open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(line + '\n')
print(len(line), 'chars')
EOF
echo ok

content.content: 175:- F-132 **Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit, as the specification says.** It builds P-73. Every arithmetic operation on a fixed width whose result can leave its type raises it, `^`, `CHOOSE` and `LCM` included, and a program can catch it. Three kinds of operation raise nothing: the wrapping operators (F-130) and `narrow`, the written conversion of a `ZZ64` to `ZZ32` or an `NN64` to `NN32` (P-72), which keep the low bits; and the shifts `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT`, which lose the bits shifted out (F-125). Gated by `tests/FixedWidthOverflowRungB.fss` (`+`, `-`, `DOT` (`·`), `DIV`, negation and absolute value, on the four fixed widths) and `tests/PowChooseLcmRungE.fss` (`^`, `CHOOSE` and `LCM`). The compiled path is outside this fact. Its known gaps: the compiler prelude's ranges raise `IntegerOverflow` where their bounds sum beyond `ZZ32` (row 453); `^` saturates, throws an uncatchable Java exception or adds (rows 523 to 525); and `CHOOSE` past its helper's table dies with a Java exception (row 521). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overflow-natives/REPORT.md` section 13; `compile-ladder/rung-size-range/REPORT.md` section 12.

content.content:
F-306: added
- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). A native bound to a helper of `nativeHelpers/` raises the library's own exception where the helper raises a class of the compiled prelude, such as `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$DivisionByZero`, so `ZZ32`'s `DIV` by zero raises `DivisionByZero` (F-299). content.content: - F-299 **Walk loads a `builtinPrimitive` string that names a static helper of `nativeHelpers/` beside its glue classes, and 97 of the one library's 449 live bindings name one.** The loader (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java`, reached from `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative`, `interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:194-201`) takes the helper's overload whose Java parameter and result types carry the declared types, `self` first, carries each value at its declared type, and refuses at load a string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` that names no static method, fits no overload, or has a declared parameter or result type that no Java type carries. It reads a method's `self` only by the helper's Java type, so a binding in a method of a program's own type loads (row 847). It raises a helper's `fortress.<Api>$<Name>` as the library's `<Name>`. The 97: 20 of trait `ZZ32`'s operators and functions, its `CHOOSE` among them (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:741-810`; F-305), 21 of trait `ZZ64`'s, its `CHOOSE` among them (`:831-905`), and 16 of trait `ZZ`'s (`:1007-1076`; F-306), `Int`'s `asString` and `asExprString` (`LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:371`, `:373`), `Float`'s 30 (F-303), and the small rest's eight (F-307); the other 352 still name glue classes. With F-298 the compiled checker reads the 97 against their helpers' Java signatures from this step on (P-58). A native over `String`, helper or glue class alike, receives a non-flat string's type name (row 846). Test: `tests/NativeHelperBindingWalk.fss`, with `NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk`, `NativeHelperRaiseWalk`, `NativeHelperMisspeltWalk`, `NativeHelperMisfitWalk`, `NativeHelperUncarriedWalk`, `ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk`, `NativeHelperFamilyIntegersWalk`, `ZZ64DivisionByZeroWalk` and `ZZDivisionByZeroWalk`. content.content:
- F-34 **Under the switch-over's setting the code generator refuses 52 declarations of the library's twelve components, all of them declarations that the checker passes.** Measured once on climb batch 22's code (`2bff2fe23`), with the checker's failures caught per declaration and the bound `Any`, the distance stage's setting: `FortressLibrary` 28, `RangeInternals` 11, `List` and `String` 5 each, and `FlatString`, `Stream` and `NatReflect` 1 each. A declaration counts at its first wall, and no emitted class was run, so after the switch-over the code generator stands between the library and bytecode at 52 declarations at least. Each kind has a ledger row; the kinds include a local function (row 304), varargs (row 624), `asif` (row 818), "Not in the trait table" (row 733) and a header `where` clause (row 701). On climb batch 21b's base (`aa5c67d48`) the dispatch generator refused none of `FortressLibrary`'s 178 overload sets. No test checks it, since the gate's distance stage runs no code generation. Detail: `reviews/phase3-exit/zero-audit.md`, "Part C. The debt carried into phase 4", item 4; `perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, sections 2 to 6.

- F-281 **The compiled checker checks the overloading of every operator, symbolic ones included; with them checked, the distance and the count are 0, with no crash (F-53).** Its three loops, over the top-level set, a trait's provided methods and their overriding return types, read `isCheckedName`, which admits every operator (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:766-773`); the export check reads every operator too, each under its declared name only (F-287). An on-demand import adds an api's declarations once, and leaves out a name its `except` clause lists; the check still reads an on-demand api's declaration of a name the component imports by name from another api (row 813), and an `except` that lists an operator leaves it imported on both paths (row 814). Outside its trait, a self type whose `comprises` clause lists types at a `where`-clause variable is read as the trait type (`TypeAnalyzer.selfComprised`), so `AnyList`'s `||` is checked; such a program still stops in the code generator (row 812; row 701). So the distance stage is the full check of F-245. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXSymbolicOperatorOverloadUnrelated`, `ComprisesWhereFunctionalMethodChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereFunctionalMethodBounds`, `OperatorPrefixInfixImport` and `ImportExceptOverload`, and by the stages ('#total 0', '#crash none'; '#total 0'). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-symbolic-check/REPORT.md` sections 1, 3 and 5.

- F-270 **The compiled checker opens a value of a trait whose `comprises` clause lists a type at a `where`-clause size: it gives each listed type's `nat` and `int` `where`-clause sizes a fresh name for the call.** In `trait NatParam comprises { N[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]`, a `NatParam` passed where `N[\$n\]` is expected, `$n` being the checker's inference variable for the called function's size parameter, binds `$n` to the fresh size, and the call's result type carries it. An opened size is not known to differ from any size. Walk's `comprises` check at load reads such a size as any size, the same at each of its places; at a call, walk binds the argument's own size. This is way 4a of fork 3 of the array design, a size known only at run time: the checker reads such a size as fixed for that call, not as unknown. P-85 leaves the array design's three questions open with no default; the third stands on this ground, and way 4a is the one way built on it. The code generator does not compile such a trait: "Can't compile TraitDecl NatParamT" (row 307; `compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun`). In row 682's program, with `trait NatParamT comprises { Nt[\n\] } where [\nat n\]`, the checker refuses `f(x: NatParamT)` beside `f[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\])` as two declarations of one parameter type, where walk runs the pair (row 682, contested). F-251 holds the same opening for a type variable. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatOpenChecker`, and under walk by `tests/NatOpenWalk` and `NatOpenUnlistedExtender`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-expressions/REPORT.md` section 1, "Fork 3, way 4a, under Q13.3", and section 12.

- F-181 **The code generator refuses every function, method, object and trait declaration that carries a `where` clause in its own header, and every function or method with a contract (row 701).** A `where` clause on an `extends` entry, and a trait's or object's contract, do not reach this refusal; F-255 says how each path reads them (rows 774 and 781). The `fortress-repo` skill's `references/compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet", gives this refusal and the constructs that the code generator has no case for, a local function among them (row 304). An array comprehension has no case either. In a probe, a scratch copy of `CodeGen.java` let a `where` clause that only binds static parameters past the trait guard. A component with a trait of the shape of the library's `NatParam`, `trait NatP comprises { Nn[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]`, then compiled and ran; its clause binds a size and states no constraint. `compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun`, which reads such a value's size from its run-time descriptor at a call, compiled and failed verification (row 307). Detail: `coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md` section 3; `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.7 (the probe).

juxtaposition, \EXP{\dottimes}, \EXP{\div}, \OPR{BITAND}, \OPR{BITOR},
\OPR{BITXOR}, \OPR{BITNOT} and \OPR{CHOOSE} of the traits \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}
and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, with the functions \VAR{widen} and \VAR{unsigned} of
the first and \VAR{narrow}, \VAR{unsigned} and \VAR{big} of the second, and the
same operators but \EXP{<} and \OPR{CHOOSE} of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}};
eighteen bindings of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and of the interpreter's
objects twenty-one of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, forty of \TYP{Char} and thirty of
\TYP{Float}; the getters \VAR{asString} and \VAR{asExprString} of the
interpreter's objects \TYP{Int}, \TYP{Long} and \TYP{BigNum}; and the function
\VAR{char}.

Until the compiled code moves onto \library, the type checker checks the moved
bindings, but no compiled program runs them.
Where a binding declares \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} or \TYP{Char}
at a position at which its helper takes or answers a Java \texttt{int} or
\texttt{long}, the compiler composes the call with one of six transfer helpers
at that position, as the compiled library writes its own operations on those
types, and the type checker checks the composition.
Under the interpreter a helper's raise of \TYP{IntegerOverflow} or
\TYP{DivisionByZero} is the library's own exception, so \EXP{\div} by zero on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}
and \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}, as \chapref{operators}
says of an integer result; \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD}, which still name glue
classes, end the run with a Java exception at a divisor of zero, on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} (row~336 of the revival's gap
ledger) and on \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}
(row~848 of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter passes a helper declared over \TYP{String}, as its glue classes
do, the name of the value's type in place of its characters where the value is
not a flat string, as a \TYP{String} made by concatenating two long strings
(row~846 of the revival's gap ledger).
For a method, the interpreter is told the type that declares it: it refuses at
load a helper bound in a method of a type that no Java type carries, as a
program's own object, and takes only an overload whose first Java parameter
carries that type, which it reads by the type's name, for the types of
\library\ whose names no program can give its own types.
It refuses such a binding in a dotted method of a generic trait or object only
where an instance's method is made, so a program that makes no instance loads
(row~864 of the revival's gap ledger); and it reads the declaring type, not the
value's, so a program's object that extends a carried trait of \library\
against its \KWD{comprises} clause, which the interpreter loads (row~551 of the
revival's gap ledger), still reaches the helper with a value that no Java type
carries.
The compiler leaves a declaration with a varargs parameter as a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, so the type checker does not check such a binding
against its helper (row~849 of the revival's gap ledger); no binding of
\library\ that names a helper has a varargs parameter.
Nor does it rewrite such a body in a local function or in a method of an object
expression, which stays a call of \VAR{builtinPrimitive} and does not compile
(row~865 of the revival's gap ledger); \library\ has no binding in either.
"""
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print(len(old), len(new))
EOF
